messages:
emma_ml: Kicked off a regional slabbench comparing A100 vs H100 for the new 13B open model (mixed workloads: chat prompts w/ 48 token prefill + 256 token decode). Goal: p50/p95 prefill & decode latency, tokens/sec, and $/1M tokens across us-east1 / eu-west1 / asia-southeast1. Link to dashboard: https://dash.internal/r/slabbench-2364809123 :mag:
jonah_infra: Ran baseline across stock kernels and int8 quant. Quick numbers (avg of 10 runs / region):
```
Region      | GPU  | prefill_p50(ms) | decode_p50(ms) | tok/s | $/1M tok
us-east1    | A100 | 36              | 42             | 9.2   | 9.8
us-east1    | H100 | 30              | 36             | 11.1  | 8.4
eu-west1    | A100 | 38              | 45             | 8.7   | 11.3
eu-west1    | H100 | 33              | 39             | 10.2  | 9.6
asia-southe | A100 | 48              | 62             | 6.5   | 14.0
asia-southe | H100 | 41              | 52             | 7.8   | 12.1
```
Notes: A100 numbers include small tail spikes when kernel falls back to generic matmul at seq_len>384. H100 used cuSparse kernels where available.
kai_perf: Interesting — did you see kernel fallthrough logs? That explains p95 tail. Also try enabling continuous-batching delta=8 and set kernel_prefer=hopper-optim in the runtime config for H100 to force preferred kernels. I saw 8-12% tok/s improvement when we forced the hopper path on similar models.
anya_research: Quality check: ran eval on 2k prompts (generation overlap + BLEU-ish heuristics) — int8 quant on A100 kept ~99.6% pass vs baseline, but on H100 with nv-optimized kernels we see a small mismatch in prefix logits leading to 0.7% degradation in exact-match for a deterministic subset. Suspect fp16->int8 cast ordering in the custom kernel. Filing issue: ML-1248.
maria_prod: Costing: those $/1M tok assume 3:1 multiplexing and reserved pricing on Dedicated. If you switch to burst instances with on-demand H100 the cost goes +35%. We should include Dedicated vs On-demand columns next pass.
jonah_infra: ops-bot completed sweep logs: https://s3.internal/benchlogs/2364809123.tar.gz :white_check_mark: Attached kernel trace excerpt:
```
[2026-03-18T12:04:32Z] kernel_select: hopper_mha_v2 applied (seq=256)
[2026-03-18T12:04:34Z] kernel_select: fallback generic_gemm (seq=512)
[2026-03-18T12:04:34Z] runtime: kv_cache hit ratio 0.74
```
kai_perf: For the next run let's do: 1) force hopper_mha for seq up to 1024, 2) try nf4 vs int8x4 quant for H100, 3) run p99 tailbench with microbursts (qps spikes 10->100 for 30s). I can script this tonight.
emma_ml: Perfect. Also add a quality gate: any config that drops deterministic exact-match >0.3% fails the bring-up. @anya_research will run the eval suite automatically after each sweep.
ops-bot: benchmark-bot: sweep 2364809123 completed. Artifacts: /artifacts/slabbench/2364809123. Summary: H100 wins on tok/s and $/1M in US/EU; performance gap shrinks in APAC due to instance latency.
